items.title: ISRO — Evolution, Organisation & Launch Vehicles
items.body:
## Evolution

- **INCOSPAR** (Indian National Committee for Space Research) set up **1962** under **Vikram Sarabhai** (father of Indian space programme); reorganised as **ISRO on 15 August 1969**.
- **Department of Space (DoS)** and the Space Commission created **1972**; ISRO works under DoS.
- Early leadership: **Sarabhai** (vision), **Satish Dhawan** (institution-building), later **U R Rao, Kasturirangan, K. Sivan, S. Somanath**.

## Launch vehicles

| Vehicle | Role / payload |
|---|---|
| SLV-3, ASLV | Early experimental launchers |
| **PSLV** | Workhorse — LEO/SSO, interplanetary injection (Chandrayaan-1, MOM) |
| **GSLV** | GEO comsats; indigenous cryogenic upper stage |
| **LVM3 (GSLV Mk-III)** | Heaviest operational; Chandrayaan-3, Gaganyaan |
| **SSLV** | Small sats (~500 kg) to LEO; 'launch-on-demand' |
| NGLV | Next-gen heavy-lift, under development |

## Applications (societal)

- Communication & broadcasting (INSAT/GSAT), remote sensing (IRS), navigation (NavIC), plus tele-education, telemedicine, weather forecasting, disaster warning, cartography and resource mapping.
keyPoints: INCOSPAR (1962) under Vikram Sarabhai became ISRO on 15 August 1969; Department of Space created 1972.
PSLV is ISRO's workhorse (Chandrayaan-1, MOM); LVM3/GSLV Mk-III is the heaviest operational launcher.
SSLV serves small satellites (~500 kg) to LEO; NGLV is the next-gen heavy-lift vehicle under development.
Satellite families: INSAT/GSAT (communication), IRS (remote sensing), NavIC (navigation).
Applications include tele-education, telemedicine, weather, disaster warning and cartography.

items.title: Flagship Missions — Chandrayaan, Aditya, Gaganyaan, SpaDeX, NISAR
items.body:
## Recent flagship missions

- **Chandrayaan-3 (23 Aug 2023):** first soft landing near the **lunar south pole**; India became the **4th nation** to soft-land on the Moon. Lander **Vikram**, rover **Pragyan**, site **Shiv Shakti Point**.
- **Aditya-L1:** India's first solar mission; launched 2 Sep 2023, inserted into a **halo orbit around Sun-Earth L1** on 6 Jan 2024 (~1.5 million km from Earth); key payload VELC.
- **Gaganyaan:** human spaceflight — 3 crew to ~400 km LEO on human-rated **LVM3**. **TV-D1 (Oct 2023)** tested the crew-escape system; four IAF pilots named as astronaut-designates (Feb 2024); uncrewed flights precede the crewed flight (targeted 2026–27).
- **SpaDeX:** launched PSLV-C60 (30 Dec 2024); **docking achieved 16 Jan 2025**, making India the **4th nation** to demonstrate in-space docking — key for BAS and Chandrayaan-4.
- **NISAR (30 Jul 2025):** ISRO-NASA Earth-observation satellite; first with **dual-frequency (L & S band) SAR**; monitors land/ice deformation, ecosystems and hazards.

## Future / vision

- **Chandrayaan-4** (lunar sample return, ~2028), **Shukrayaan** (Venus orbiter), **Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035**, **Indian on the Moon by 2040**.
keyPoints: Chandrayaan-3 (23 Aug 2023): first south-pole soft landing; lander Vikram, rover Pragyan, site Shiv Shakti Point.
Aditya-L1 reached a halo orbit around Sun-Earth L1 on 6 Jan 2024 — India's first solar mission.
Gaganyaan: 3 crew to LEO on human-rated LVM3; TV-D1 (2023) tested crew escape; crew named Feb 2024.
SpaDeX achieved India's first in-space docking on 16 Jan 2025 — the 4th nation to do so.
NISAR (Jul 2025) is the ISRO-NASA dual-frequency (L & S band) SAR Earth-observation satellite.
Vision: Chandrayaan-4 sample return (~2028), Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035, Indian on Moon by 2040.
items.mnemonic: Order of recent firsts: 'C-A-G-S-N' = Chandrayaan-3 → Aditya → Gaganyaan test → SpaDeX → NISAR.

items.title: NavIC, Private Space & Sriharikota (AP)
items.body:
## NavIC (IRNSS)

- Autonomous **regional** navigation system covering **India + ~1,500 km** around it (extendable), unlike the global GPS/GLONASS/Galileo/BeiDou. The operational constellation is designed around **7 satellites** (3 geostationary + 4 geosynchronous), built and operated by **ISRO**.
- Offers Standard Positioning (civilian) and Restricted services; newer satellites add the **L1 signal** for smartphones.

## Private & commercial space

- **IN-SPACe** — single-window promoter/authoriser for private space activity.
- **NSIL (New Space India Limited)** — ISRO's commercial arm.
- Start-ups: **Skyroot** (Vikram-S, India's first private rocket, 2022), **Agnikul** (Agnibaan, 3D-printed engine).

## Sriharikota — SDSC-SHAR (Andhra Pradesh)

- India's primary **spaceport** on the Bay of Bengal coast; launch site for PSLV, GSLV, LVM3.
- Near-equatorial coastal location aids **eastward launches** with safe over-sea trajectories; named after **Satish Dhawan**.
- A **second spaceport** (Kulasekarapattinam, Tamil Nadu) is being built for SSLV — but SHAR remains AP's strategic space asset.
keyPoints: NavIC/IRNSS is a regional system (7-satellite constellation) covering India + ~1,500 km, unlike global GPS; newer satellites add the L1 civilian signal.
IN-SPACe authorises/promotes private space; NSIL is ISRO's commercial arm.
Skyroot's Vikram-S (2022) was India's first private rocket; Agnikul builds the Agnibaan with a 3D-printed engine.
SDSC-SHAR at Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh is India's primary spaceport for PSLV/GSLV/LVM3.
Sriharikota's near-equatorial east-coast location enables efficient, safe eastward launches.

items.title: DRDO & the Missile Arsenal (IGMDP)
items.body:
## DRDO

- **Defence Research and Development Organisation**, formed **1958**; premier defence R&D body with 50+ labs under the Department of Defence R&D.
- Runs the **Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP)**, launched **1983** under **A.P.J. Abdul Kalam**.

## Key missiles

| Missile | Category |
|---|---|
| **Prithvi** | Short-range surface-to-surface ballistic |
| **Agni** | Medium-to-ICBM-class ballistic (Agni-V 5,000+ km, **MIRV** via Mission Divyastra 2024) |
| **Akash** | Medium-range surface-to-air |
| **Astra** | Beyond-visual-range air-to-air |
| **Nag** | Anti-tank guided |
| **BrahMos** | Supersonic cruise (Indo-Russian, ~Mach 2.8) |

## Strategic capabilities

- **Mission Shakti (2019):** ASAT interception in LEO — India the 4th such nation.
- **Ballistic Missile Defence (BMD):** two-tier (exo/endo-atmospheric) interceptors.
- **Hypersonics:** HSTDV demonstrator; long-range hypersonic missile tests.
- **Sea leg:** K-series SLBMs (K-15, K-4) for the nuclear triad.
keyPoints: DRDO (formed 1958) runs the IGMDP (1983), spearheaded by A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
IGMDP missiles: Prithvi (SS ballistic), Agni (ballistic), Akash (SAM), Trishul (SAM), Nag (anti-tank).
Agni-V (5,000+ km) tested MIRV under Mission Divyastra (March 2024).
BrahMos is an Indo-Russian supersonic cruise missile (~Mach 2.8), land/sea/sub/air-launched.
Mission Shakti (2019) demonstrated ASAT; DRDO also pursues two-tier BMD and HSTDV hypersonics.
items.mnemonic: IGMDP missiles = 'PATNA' → Prithvi, Agni, Trishul, Nag, Akash.

items.title: Defence Indigenisation & Operation Sindoor (2025)
items.body:
## Self-reliance in defence (Atmanirbhar Bharat)

- **Indigenous platforms:** **Tejas** (Light Combat Aircraft, HAL), **Arjun** (main battle tank), Dhruv/Prachand helicopters, indigenous aircraft carrier **INS Vikrant**.
- **Policy levers:** **Defence Acquisition Procedure (DAP) 2020** prioritising **'Buy (Indian-IDDM)'**; **iDEX** funding defence start-ups/MSMEs; **positive indigenisation lists** restricting specified imports; rising defence-export figures.

## Operation Sindoor (7 May 2025)

- Indian military operation launching **precision strikes on cross-border terror infrastructure** after the Pahalgam attack (Apr 2025).
- Demonstrated a **layered, integrated air-defence** response — the **S-400** system (inducted as 'Sudarshan Chakra'), indigenous **Akash** SAMs and counter-drone systems working in a networked command.
- Reinforced the strategic case for **indigenous air defence, drones and long-range precision munitions** (incl. BrahMos), feeding the Atmanirbhar Bharat push.

## Mains angle

- Balance strategic autonomy vs import dependence; dual-use of space/defence tech; ethics of autonomous/space weaponisation; AP's stake via Sriharikota and defence-manufacturing corridors.
keyPoints: Indigenous platforms: Tejas LCA (HAL), Arjun MBT, INS Vikrant carrier.
DAP 2020 prioritises 'Buy (Indian-IDDM)'; iDEX funds defence start-ups; positive indigenisation lists curb imports.
Operation Sindoor (7 May 2025) followed the Pahalgam attack — precision strikes with layered air defence.
It showcased integrated air defence: S-400 ('Sudarshan Chakra'), Akash SAM and counter-drone systems.
Mains angle: strategic autonomy vs imports, dual-use tech, and AP's stake via Sriharikota.
items.source: Ministry of Defence — DAP 2020/iDEX; PIB — Operation Sindoor (2025)

items.title: Andhra Pradesh — Space & Atmospheric Science Assets
items.body:
## Sriharikota (SDSC-SHAR)

- **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR)** sits on **Sriharikota**, a barrier island separating **Pulicat Lake** from the Bay of Bengal — India's **primary orbital spaceport**.
- **NVS-02** (GSLV-F15) launched **29 Jan 2025** was the **100th launch from Sriharikota**; NVS-02 is a **second-generation NavIC** satellite.

## Other AP S&T assets

| Facility | Place | Focus |
|---|---|---|
| NARL | Gadanki (near Tirupati) | Atmospheric/space research; MST radar |
| NSTL (DRDO) | Visakhapatnam | Underwater weapons |

## Private space

- **Skyroot Vikram-S** (2022) = India's first private rocket (sub-orbital). **Vikram-1** = orbital-class launcher; private orbital launch from Sriharikota slated for **2026**. **IN-SPACe** authorises private activity; **NSIL** is ISRO's commercial arm.
keyPoints: SDSC-SHAR is on Sriharikota island (Pulicat Lake / Bay of Bengal) — India's primary orbital spaceport.
NVS-02 (GSLV-F15, 29 Jan 2025) was the 100th launch from Sriharikota; a 2nd-gen NavIC satellite.
NARL, Gadanki (near Tirupati) does atmospheric/space research with its MST radar.
Vikram-S (2022) was India's first private rocket; Vikram-1 is Skyroot's orbital-class vehicle.
IN-SPACe regulates/promotes private space; NSIL is ISRO's commercial arm.
